\\n\\ud83d\\udcdd Walkthrough\\n\\n## Walkthrough\\n\\nAdds combo rarity, unlock cost, and level progression to combos; new ScriptableObjects and editor tooling for rarity data; Memory gains unlock/level persistence helpers; UI updated to render locked/special combos via a new SpecialComboCell and rarity visuals.\\n\\n## Changes\\n\\n|Cohort / File(s)|Summary|\\n|---|---|\\n|**Core Combo Definition**
`Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboDefinition.cs`|Added `ERarityEnum` (Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic), `UnlockCost`, `Rarity`, `LevelMultipliers`, and computed properties `Locked`, `Level`, `MaxLevel` backed by `Memory` helpers.|\\n|**Rarity Data Infrastructure**
`Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboRarityData.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboRarityDefinition.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboCellRarityData.cs`|New ScriptableObjects: `ComboRarityData` (singleton, editor FillComboRarities), `ComboRarityDefinition` (level requirements), and `CombosCellRarityData`/`ComboCellRarityData` (rarity display data and reset on load).|\\n|**Memory Persistence**
`Assets/Scripts/Helper/Memory.cs`|Added `IsComboUnlocked`, `UnlockCombo`, `GetComboLevel`, and `IncreaseComboLevel` to persist and query combo unlock state and levels.|\\n|**UI & Cells**
`Assets/Scripts/UI/ComboScreen.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/UI/SpecialComboCell.cs`|`ComboScreen` conditionally instantiates a `SpecialComboCell` for locked or non-Common combos; `LockedComboCell` renamed/refactored to `SpecialComboCell`, uses a `SerializedDictionary` for visuals, handles unlock flow and currency updates.|\\n|**Assets / Meta**
`Assets/Resources/Combos/*`, `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/*.meta`, `Assets/Resources/Combos/*.asset.meta`, `Assets/Art/Textures/UI/*.meta`|Added folder/meta entries and asset meta files for rarity assets and new scriptable object meta files; new texture meta entries for rare backgrounds/frames.|\\n\\n## Sequence Diagram\\n\\n```mermaid\\nsequenceDiagram\\n participant ComboScreen as ComboScreen\\n participant ComboDefinition as ComboDefinition\\n participant Memory as Memory\\n participant SpecialComboCell as SpecialComboCell\\n participant RarityData as CombosCellRarityData\\n\\n ComboScreen->>ComboDefinition: read Locked, Rarity\\n ComboDefinition->>Memory: IsComboUnlocked(name)\\n Memory-->>ComboDefinition: unlocked/locked\\n\\n alt Locked or Rarity != Common\\n ComboScreen->>SpecialComboCell: Instantiate _specialPrefab\\n SpecialComboCell->>ComboDefinition: evaluate Locked\\n alt Locked\\n SpecialComboCell->>RarityData: request visuals for Rarity\\n RarityData-->>SpecialComboCell: return sprites/text\\n SpecialComboCell->>Memory: UnlockCombo(name) [on user action]\\n Memory-->>SpecialComboCell: persist result\\n else Unlocked (special)\\n SpecialComboCell->>RarityData: request visuals for Rarity\\n RarityData-->>SpecialComboCell: return sprites/text\\n end\\n else Common & Unlocked\\n ComboScreen->>ComboScreen: Instantiate regular cell and add to list\\n end\\n```\\n\\n## Estimated Code Review Effort\\n\\n\\ud83c\\udfaf 3 (Moderate) | \\u23f1\\ufe0f ~22 minutes\\n\\n## Poem\\n\\n> \\ud83d\\udc30 I munched the code in twilight's glow, \\n> > Rarities shimmer, seeds now sow, \\n> > Locks click open with a little clack, \\n> > Multipliers hop the damage track, \\n> > A rabbit cheers \\u2014 combos on the go!\\n\\n
\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\n> [!NOTE]\\n>
\\n> \\ud83c\\udf81 Summarized by CodeRabbit Free\\n> \\n> Your organization is on the Free plan. CodeRabbit will generate a high-level summary and a walkthrough for each pull request. For a comprehensive line-by-line review, please upgrade your subscription to CodeRabbit Pro by visiting .\\n> \\n>
\\n\\nComment `@PERSON_6026_GITHUB_USERNAME help` to get the list of available commands and usage tips.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\", \"created_at\": \"2026-02-12T06:31:12Z\"}]"}

Here is the 1st part based on the level they are within the game.

Level 1-50 = 0% bonus to monster HP

Level 51-100 = 5% bonus to monster HP

Level 101-150 = 10% bonus to monster HP

Every 50 levels from here on out = 5% more.

Here is the 2nd part on scaling monster HP based on player's tier. Each player starts at tier 0 when they first enter the game, but can move up and down tiers based on their win/loss record.

Optimize your spaces and combo connections.\\nGain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.\\nWhen the game ends, the player can upgrade the hero's Max HP, HP regen rate during the game, and attack power.\\nGame Objective:\\nDefeat all the waves of monsters in each level.\\nFailure Condition:\\nThe player\\u2019s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.\\n3. Game Flow\\nHome Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.\\nGameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.\\nResult Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.\\nUpgrades: Hero\\u2019s Max HP, HP regen rate, hero\\u2019s attack power bonus\\n4. Level Design\\n35 hand crafted levels in MVP\\nMonsters will have increased HP and attack damage as level progresses.\\nLevels will have obstacles on the board to create difficulty. These obstacles can be removed with silver earned in the level. These obstacles reset each game.\\nLevels will have different starting points for first combo piece placement. Each level will also have a set of possible pieces that can be dropped and their drop rate.\\n5. Art & Visual Style\\nThe top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.\\nDuring intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.\\nCharacter Designs: Simple Chibi style 3D characters.\\nUI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.\\n6. Audio\\nMusic: None\\nSFX: Standard fighting sounds.\\n7. Monetization\\nAds: None in MVP\\n8. Ugly Game Mockups\\nHome Screen with 3 upgrade choices, start button, coin balance and settings button\\nGameplay\\nGame Starts, 3 pieces randomly selected for players to choose from.\\nPlayers drag pieces onto the board, the character starts doing loop animation of the attacks on the board.\\nThe values showing total punch, kick and special attack power changes real time based on pieces on the board\\nThe dmg/s calculation also updates real time as pieces are being placed\\nThe Info button will bring up a pop up of available moves (see below)\\nPressing refresh will consume gold if available, and refreshes the 3 cards.\\nHolding a tile under the finger will change the refresh button to SELL. If a player moves pieces over the sell button, the piece will be sold.\\nCoin balance and health is displayed near the top\\nAfter pressing the fight button, the camera shifts upward to increase the size of the fight scene and the battle starts. Starting A Level\\nLevel starts with a 6x6 empty game board.\\nThe level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.\\nPlayers are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.\\nTiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.\\nOnce the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 Special attack (fireball) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 repeat\\nWhen the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.\\nIf There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)\\nFireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.\\nPlayers will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.\\nWhen the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.\\nThe game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.\\nPLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..\\nBlock Merging & Rearrangement\\nWhen the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.\\nHolding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.\\nWhen the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.\\nLike the video below.\\nScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4\\nWhile arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.\\nThe only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.\\nOnce players decide to continue fighting, clicking the \\u201cFight\\u201d button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.\\nPlayers can merge the blocks in the bottom part.\\n2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation\\nThere are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.\\nTiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.\\nTiles will come in different shapes\\nPunch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40\\nThe same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called \\u201cAssist Tiles,\\u201d they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.\\nThe individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.\\nThe damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:\\n[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier\\nThis calculates the individual action power for the combo\\nCombo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.\\nSmall sample list of combos and their multiplier and base DPS, this is accessed via the info button during the game. The character at the top animates the combo punching air/dummy when the player selects a combo.\\n3. Combo Creation UI/UX\\n4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades\\nThere will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.\\nThey will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. So for the implementation, please be aware that we can extend upgrades.\\nAttack Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) So 100% + 2% + 2% + 2% + 2% (Level 4 = 108% * attack)\\nHealth Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) Same as attack. So level 5 health increase = 110% * base HP of 100 = 110 total Hp\\nHealth Regen Increase (+0.02% per second, Additive) So level 7 is 2% base regen + (0.02% * 7 = 0.14%) final health regen = 2.14% HP regen per second.\\n5. Monsters, Stats, Damage Assignment, Stagger and Loot\\nEach monster when hit is \\u201cstunned\\u201d for 0.25 seconds. However this has a cooldown of 1.5 seconds. This means after being stunned, the earliest the next time the same monster can be stunned again is 1.25 seconds later because 1.5 second cooldown from first stun - 0.25 stun duration = 1.25 seconds after end of first stun.\\nMonster attack animation should be from start to finish should be 1 second, with damage dealt at 0.8 second timestamp\\nWe do not need more than 5 monsters for MVP\\nWhen monsters are hit, we display damage dealt using standard RPG text VFX. We then display the monster health bar permanently above their head, but we do not display numerical values for their HP\\nMonster speed is the second it takes to move from edge of screen to crossing the monster attack line. Attack speed is expressed in seconds per attack.\\n| Monster Name | Base HP | Damage | Seconds Per Attack | Move Speed |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| [USERNAME_37755] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n| [USERNAME_53102] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n| [USERNAME_53103] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n| [USERNAME_53104] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n| [USERNAME_53105] | 10 | 10 | 1 | 10 |\\n6. Levels\\nWe need to let designers designate starting positions for each level.\\nEach level will also have obstacles that need to be removed via silver.\\nEach level will have 15 waves of monsters\\nEach wave of monsters will get an HP and damage multiplier bonus following a standard algorithm\\nHP multiplier for monster is wave # * XXX\\nDamage multiplier for monster is wave # * YYY\\nWe need to utilize the monster spawning system from Zombie Match, this will allow designers to specify monsters spawn timing and quantity\\nLevel Design Tools\\nEach level will have monsters, monsters spawn, their stats, board type, and the pool of tiles available.\\nSo what\\u2019s needed from a level is that\\nLEVEL NAME\\nMonster Track\\nWaves\\nMonster type,\\nMonster amount,\\nSpawn Duration (fixed or interval)\\n[USERNAME_5859]\\u2019s stats (dmg & HP)\\nWave multiplier for damage & HP (separate)\\nAnother wave\\nMonster type,\\nMonster amount,\\nSpawn Duration (fixed or interval)\\n[USERNAME_5859]\\u2019s stats (dmg & HP)\\nWave multiplier for damage & HP (separate)\\nBoard Info\\nPool of tiles\\nAbility to select available tiles used in that level\\nSpawn rate of individual tiles\\nSpawn rate of colors (?)\\nSpawn rate of shapes (?)\\nPool types (if necessary later on)\\nStart and exit nodes  (if necessary later on)\\n7. Player Starting Stats\\nBase player HP is 100\\nBase player regen rate is 2% per second, but this is only during the \\u201cfight\\u201d phase and not the prep phase.\\nBase attack is 0, no tiles placed = no damage.\\n8. Experience Table and Skill Choices\\nFor XP tables Combo Fighter Design Details\\nFor Silver Tables Combo Fighter Design Details\\nXP and Silver.png\\nExperience points will reset after each attempt, meaning that it will start from the scratch in every level attempt.\\nExperience will be gained from the actions below,\\nMerging blocks yield less XP\\nKilling enemies yields more XP\\nRoguelite skills don't require any currency to use. Just selecting the desired one out of all 3 options.\\nThe skills will have 3 phases that can be improved further after selecting the first phase.\\nRoguelite Skills In MVP\\nIncrease Punch Damage by 35%   (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +35% regardless of level is a better start.\\nIncrease Kick Damage by 20%   (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +20% regardless of level is a better start.\\nIncrease Special Attack Damage by 15%   (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +15% regardless of level is a better start.\\nIncrease All Damage by 10%  (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) I think this one should scale.\\nLevel 1 +10%\\nLevel 2 +15%\\nLevel 3 +20%\\nLevel 4 +25%\\nLevel 5 +30%\\nIncrease Max HP by 50% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +50% regardless of level is a better start.\\nReduce Attack Cooldown by 20% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But I think max 2 levels is enough for this:\\nLevel 1 Reduce Attack Cooldown by 20%\\nLevel 2 Reduce Attack Cooldown by 30%\\nThis means by level 2, the player will have 20% + 30% cooldown. The pause between combos will be half as long.\\nRestore 100% HP (No levels, but can be repeatedly chosen, if it appears)\\nIncrease HP Regen by 1% / sec (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nRestore +1 HP Per Enemy Hit (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nGain 60 Silver (I think when this skill appears, it should have the rewarded amount = the last wave player has finished rewarded amount)\\nGain X Gold (Can only be obtained ONCE per run, This should always be 50% of the level reward)\\nLevel Up a Random Tile (Can be repeatedly chosen)\\nSlow Enemies Move Speed by 15% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nGet 1 Free Refresh\\nIncrease Tile Merging Exp by 25% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nIncrease Monster Exp by 25% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nIncrease All XP gained by 10% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nIncrease Assist Tile Power by 20% (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nDamage Immunity for 5 seconds (Deprecated)\\nGet a Level 2 Small Square P/K/S Tile (3 variants to this, tile will appear automatically on board, if board is full it appears in staging slots, if slots also full, it will appear in the very next refresh) SKIP FOR ALPHA\\nFireball Can Hit 3 Additional Enemies (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nCombos with 4 Hits or Less Gains 15% Bonus Damage (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\nCombos with 5+ Hits Gains 20% Bonus Damage (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.)\\n9. Combo List and their Bonus Multipliers\\nHere\\n10. VFX and animations\\nCombo tile VFX when character is attacking.\\n11. Mechanics Spreadsheet link: HERE\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_8fb667cfb8d1e8dcc7a182", "title": "Combo Fighter GDD", "revisionId": "8fb667cfb8", "text": "Overview
1. Game Overview
Title: Combo Fighter
Genre: Merge puzzle auto battler
Platform: (iOS / Android)
Core Loop Summary:
Place fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.
2. Core Gameplay
Player Actions:
Drag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.
Draw additional pieces randomly to place them on the board. Optimize your spaces and combo connections.
Gain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.
When the game ends, the player can upgrade the hero's Max HP, HP regen rate during the game, and attack power.
Game Objective:
Defeat all the waves of monsters in each level.
Failure Condition:
The player’s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.
3. Game Flow
Home Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.
Gameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.
Result Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.
Upgrades: Hero’s Max HP, HP regen rate, hero’s attack power bonus
4. Level Design
35 hand crafted levels in MVP
Monsters will have increased HP and attack damage as level progresses.
Levels will have obstacles on the board to create difficulty. These obstacles can be removed with silver earned in the level. These obstacles reset each game.
Levels will have different starting points for first combo piece placement. Each level will also have a set of possible pieces that can be dropped and their drop rate.
5. Art & Visual Style
The top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.
During intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.
Character Designs: Simple Chibi style 3D characters.
UI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.
6. Audio
Music: None
SFX: Standard fighting sounds.
7. Monetization
Ads: None in MVP
8. Ugly Game Mockups
Home Screen with 3 upgrade choices, start button, coin balance and settings button
Gameplay
Game Starts, 3 pieces randomly selected for players to choose from.
Players drag pieces onto the board, the character starts doing loop animation of the attacks on the board.
The values showing total punch, kick and special attack power changes real time based on pieces on the board
The dmg/s calculation also updates real time as pieces are being placed
The Info button will bring up a pop up of available moves (see below)
Pressing refresh will consume gold if available, and refreshes the 3 cards.
Holding a tile under the finger will change the refresh button to SELL. If a player moves pieces over the sell button, the piece will be sold.
Coin balance and health is displayed near the top
After pressing the fight button, the camera shifts upward to increase the size of the fight scene and the battle starts. This phase requires no input action from the players
Info Pop Up
Simple End Game Screen
DOCUMENT DOES NOT END HERE! MAKE SURE TO CLICK ON THE OTHER TABS (“Detailed Mechanics”) IN THIS DOCUMENT ON THE LEFT SIDE BAR IN GOOGLE DOCS
Detailed Mechanics
1. Starting A Level
Level starts with a 6x6 empty game board.
The level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.
Players are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.
Tiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.
Once the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) → 0.6 second delay → Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) → 0.6 second delay → Special attack (fireball) → 0.6 second delay → repeat
When the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.
If There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)
Fireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.
Players will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.
When the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.
The game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.
PLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..
Block Merging & Rearrangement
When the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.
Holding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.
When the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.
Like the video below.
ScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4
While arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.
The only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.
Once players decide to continue fighting, clicking the “Fight” button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.
Players can merge the blocks in the bottom part.
2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation
There are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.
Tiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.
Tiles will come in different shapes
Punch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40
The same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called “Assist Tiles,” they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.
The individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.
The damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:
[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier
This calculates the individual action power for the combo
Combo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.
Small sample list of combos and their multiplier and base DPS, this is accessed via the info button during the game. The character at the top animates the combo punching air/dummy when the player selects a combo.
3. Combo Creation UI/UX
4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades
There will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.
They will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. So for the implementation, please be aware that we can extend upgrades.
Attack Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) So 100% + 2% + 2% + 2% + 2% (Level 4 = 108% * attack)
Health Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) Same as attack. So level 5 health increase = 110% * base HP of 100 = 110 total Hp
Health Regen Increase (+0.02% per second, Additive) So level 7 is 2% base regen + (0.02% * 7 = 0.14%) final health regen = 2.14% HP regen per second.
5. Monsters, Stats, Damage Assignment, Stagger and Loot
Each monster when hit is “stunned” for 0.25 seconds. However this has a cooldown of 1.5 seconds. This means after being stunned, the earliest the next time the same monster can be stunned again is 1.25 seconds later because 1.5 second cooldown from first stun - 0.25 stun duration = 1.25 seconds after end of first stun.
Monster attack animation should be from start to finish should be 1 second, with damage dealt at 0.8 second timestamp
We do not need more than 5 monsters for MVP
When monsters are hit, we display damage dealt using standard RPG text VFX. We then display the monster health bar permanently above their head, but we do not display numerical values for their HP
Monster speed is the second it takes to move from edge of screen to crossing the monster attack line. Attack speed is expressed in seconds per attack.

content.text:
The GDD confirms it: **the design docs contain no combo-rarity or unlock/level-up spec at all** — combos are defined purely by damage multipliers. The entire rarity/unlock system that shipped in PR #37 has no basis in the GDD or the balancing sheet. That answers Owen's question.

input.title: Combo-Fighters PR #37 merged with reviewer changes still requested (no sign-off)
input.description:
**Recording the state of Combo-Fighters as of the last activity (merged 2026-02-13). Not assigning — this documents what landed, per Arthur's request in #prototype.**

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #37 "Combo Definition Updates" (author: PERSON_5877_NAME, merged by Oliver Brooks 2026-02-13)
**Review state:** Oliver Brooks left a formal **CHANGES_REQUESTED** on 2026-02-12 with 7 inline comments. **No approval was ever recorded** before it was merged the next day.

**What the reviewer pushed back on (files + asks):**
- `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboDefinition.cs` — `Locked` should not be a stored field; use a computed `IsAvailable`/PlayerPrefs + `Unlock()`. Drop the `LevelMultiplierRow` class in favour of a `float[]`. Rename enum to `ERarityEnum`.
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/ComboScreen.cs` — `_specialPrefab` naming; reviewer suggested `_lockedPrefab`.
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/LockedComboCell.cs` — refactor to a `SerializedDictionary<ERarityEnum, ComboCellRarityData>` instead of per-rarity functions/switches.
- `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboRarityData.cs` / `ComboRarityDefinition.cs` — "Is this scriptable object being used?" / "Why exactly do we need this?"

**What actually landed (verified against merge commit bf4e630):** Most structural objections WERE adopted — enum renamed to `ERarityEnum`, `IsLocked`/`Level` are now computed via `ComboManager`, `LockedComboCell` became `SpecialComboCell` using a `SerializedDictionary`. So the code was largely fixed even though the review was never formally cleared.

**Still unresolved (author argued / no re-engagement):**
1. Author pushed back on the `_specialPrefab` / `SpecialComboCell` naming; reviewer never replied — naming shipped as the author decided.
2. The final `ComboDefinition` was reworked to use `ComboLevelUpData` and no longer references `ComboRarityDefinition`. Oliver's "is this used / why do we need this" was never answered — the `ComboRarityData`/`ComboRarityDefinition` SOs may now be dead/unwired. Worth confirming they aren't orphaned.

Category: **author argued the point** (some), rest silently adopted. No live-play risk identified.

input.title: Combo-Fighters PR #35 self-merged over CHANGES_REQUESTED — auth tokens still logged (security)
input.description:
**Recording state of Combo-Fighters. Not assigning — documents what landed, per Arthur's request in #prototype.**

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #35 "Blake/backend" (author + merged by: Arthur Blake, 2026-01-30 21:33)
**Review state:** Oliver Brooks left **CHANGES_REQUESTED** at 20:36; author replied and **self-merged 6 minutes later (21:33)**. No approval recorded. CodeRabbit also posted ~22 actionable items including several security findings.

**What the reviewers pushed back on (files + asks):**
- Oliver, `Assets/Store/DominoPlayerPrefs.cs` — "Can we rename this to something else?" (author replied "Yes")
- Oliver, `Assets/Scripts/UI/Profile/ProfileScreen.cs` — missing `private`; "Looks dangerous" — `_statPrefab` GameObject can be instantiated without a `ProfileStat`; make the field typed as `ProfileStat`.
- CodeRabbit (security), `Assets/AWSGameSDK/AWSGameSDKClient.cs` — remove `rawResponse` (contains `auth_token`, `refresh_token`, `guest_secret`) from `Debug.LogError`; guard `GetUserCountry()` against neutral/invariant-culture `ArgumentException`; URL-encode GET params; stray duplicate semicolon.

**What actually landed (verified against develop):**
- ✅ The `DominoPlayerPrefs` rename DID land later — the file is now `Assets/Store/HarmonyPlayerPrefs.cs`.
- ✅ GET-param URL-encoding was fixed (`Uri.EscapeDataString`).
- ❌ **STILL IN THE BUILD (develop):** `AWSGameSDKClient.cs` logs the raw login payload — including `auth_token`, `refresh_token`, and `guest_secret` — via `Debug.LogError` at TWO sites (the "user credentials not set" branch and the `catch (Exception e)` block: `...RawResponse:{rawResponse}`). This writes credentials to device logs on any login parse hiccup.
- ❌ `GetUserCountry()` still calls `new RegionInfo(CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.Name)` with no try/catch (crashes on neutral/invariant cultures).
- ❌ Duplicate `;;` on the refreshTokenExpiration assignment (cosmetic).

Category: **CodeRabbit's security objection ignored / still standing in the live-ish build.** This is the one that is actually sitting in the build. Recommend fixing the token-logging before any further release.

input.description:
**Recording state of Combo-Fighters. Not assigning — documents what landed, per Arthur's request in #prototype.**

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #26 "Added cooldown to main menu upgrade ad watch" (author: PERSON_5877_NAME, merged by Oliver Brooks 2026-01-15 17:28)
**Review state:** Oliver Brooks left **CHANGES_REQUESTED** (2026-01-15 13:36). **No approval recorded** before merge.

**What the reviewer pushed back on (files + ask):**
- Design concern (review body): the cooldown resets on level completion — "the player can enter the level, lose very quickly and return to main menu and then they will be able to watch another ad and level up again." i.e. the reset-on-loss lets players farm the upgrade-ad reward.
- `Assets/Scripts/Managers/GameController.cs` — nit: move the two `Memory` lines to `WinScreen`.

**Author response:** deflected the design concern — "@[EMPLOYEE_0016] mentioned it does not matter if the player win or lose... we should sync with him about these concerns." No evidence that sync happened on the PR; reviewer merged it himself without recording an approval.

**What actually landed (verified against merge commit 9ecdc51):**
- ❌ The exploit the reviewer flagged is **in the shipped build**: `GameController.GameRoutine` calls `Memory.SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown(reset: true)` on level completion AND `LoseScreen` resets it on loss — so a quick loss clears the 5-min cooldown and the upgrade ad can be re-watched. Since Combo Fighter is live and monetizing, this is the reviewer's exact concern still active.
- ❌ The "move to WinScreen" nit was not applied (cosmetic).

Category: **author argued/deflected the point (to a product call attributed to [EMPLOYEE_0016]); objection still standing in the build.** Recommend a product+eng decision on whether reset-on-loss is intended.

input.text:
*Combo Fighter — state of the repo audit (as of 2026-02-28).* @Arthur Blake — record of what actually landed in `harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters` and where it stood when everyone stopped. I went by what's on the branch, not just the review label. For every PR I flagged I left a note on the PR itself and raised one unassigned ticket on the Engineering board (ENG). Nothing was reopened.

*The scope:* every merged PR where a teammate asked for changes. Only three merged with the objection still open and no sign-off recorded (#37, #35, #26). One more (#19) merged with no formal sign-off but was actually fixed in code. One (#24) is the process working. Details:

────────────────────
*FLAGGED — merged with a reviewer objection still standing (comment on PR + ticket):*

*PR #35 "Blake/backend"* — author + merged by *Arthur Blake*; reviewer *Oliver Brooks*. → *ENG-2439*
• Oliver left CHANGES_REQUESTED at 20:36; it was *self-merged 6 minutes later* (21:33), no approval. CodeRabbit also raised security findings.
• *Sitting in the build right now:* `Assets/AWSGameSDK/AWSGameSDKClient.cs` logs the raw login payload — `auth_token`, `refresh_token`, `guest_secret` — to `Debug.LogError` at two spots (the "credentials not set" branch and the `catch`). Any login parse hiccup writes credentials to device logs. Confirmed still on `develop`. `GetUserCountry()` also still crashes on neutral cultures. *This is the one I'd fix before any further release.*
• To be fair: the `DominoPlayerPrefs`→`HarmonyPlayerPrefs` rename Oliver asked for *did* land in a later PR, and the URL-encoding fix landed too.

*PR #26 "cooldown to main menu upgrade ad watch"* — author *[the ads/IAP dev]*; reviewer *Oliver Brooks* (who also merged it). → *ENG-2440*
• Oliver's objection was monetization: the upgrade-ad cooldown resets when the level ends, so a player can *enter a level, lose immediately, return to menu, and re-watch the ad to keep leveling*. Author *argued the point* — deflected to a product call ("@[the PM] said it doesn't matter if you win or lose, we should sync with him"). No sync on the PR, merged anyway, no approval.
• *Sitting in the build:* confirmed in the merge commit — `GameController` resets the cooldown on win *and* `LoseScreen` resets it on loss, so the exploit Oliver flagged is live. Given the game is still taking money, worth a product+eng call on whether reset-on-loss is intended.

*PR #37 "Combo Definition Updates"* — the last thing merged, *2026-02-13*; reviewer *Oliver Brooks*. → *ENG-2438*
• Oliver left CHANGES_REQUESTED (7 inline comments on `ComboDefinition.cs`, `ComboScreen.cs`, `LockedComboCell.cs`, `ComboRarityData/Definition.cs`) — stored `Locked` field, enum naming, an unneeded row class, refactor to a dictionary, and "is this SO even used?". *No approval was ever recorded* before merge the next day.
• *What actually landed:* most of it was fixed anyway — enum became `ERarityEnum`, `IsLocked`/`Level` are computed via `ComboManager`, `LockedComboCell` became `SpecialComboCell` with a `SerializedDictionary`. Two loose ends: the author *argued* the `SpecialComboCell` naming (reviewer never replied), and the `ComboRarityData`/`ComboRarityDefinition` SOs Oliver questioned appear orphaned — the final code uses `ComboLevelUpData` and never references them. Worth confirming they're not dead weight.

────────────────────
*NOT flagged — recorded so the next person can tell the difference:*

*PR #19 "anim sequence on combo changed"* — reviewer *Oliver Brooks*. Oliver flagged a real index-out-of-range bug (`comboTiles[i + 1]` throwing on the last tile). *Nobody said a word back* — no reply, no formal approval — *but the code was actually fixed*: the merged coroutine was refactored so it never does that access. Objection did not survive into the build, so no ticket. Note left on the PR for completeness.

*PR #24 "AppLovinMAX / Rewarded Ads"* — this is the process working. Oliver requested changes twice, author responded, *Oliver APPROVED before it merged*. Left alone.

*On your "worst kind" (agreed-to change that never landed):* I didn't find one. The only clear "yes, I'll change it" agreement was the #35 rename — and that one did eventually land. Good news.

*Also worth knowing:* several sizeable PRs merged with a reviewer *requested but no review ever submitted* — IAP #34, Main Menu #28, Settings #8, combos #3, VFX #33. Not "changes requested," so not ticketed, but nobody actually reviewed them.

────────────────────
*Design-side check (Owen's question — does the spec back up what shipped):*
Short answer: the design docs *don't* back up the rarity/unlock system that shipped. The *Combo Fighter GDD* and the *Combo List* balancing sheet define combos purely by damage multipliers — there is *no* combo-rarity, unlock-cost, or per-rarity level-up spec anywhere in them. The rarity/unlock feature (PR #37) traces only to a "Combo Unlocking Specs" the PR author cited and the Slack rarity thread. And what shipped is `ERarityEnum { Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic }` — 4 tiers, *no Common* — which matches the Slack decision ("common combos = no label, four kinds") but *not* the unlocking spec as paraphrased on the PR, which described a Common tier with its own level-up table. So if the spec got pointed at in a review to justify the rarity behaviour, it doesn't actually say that — the canonical design (GDD/sheet) is silent on rarities entirely.

────────────────────
*Zombie Match board:* I went through it. The urgent items that clearly shipped are *already* Done (e.g. ZOM-291 Time Boosters). The urgent items still *open* are recent (Oct 2025) and sit in Todo / In Progress / Regression / In Validation — labelled "Hot Fix - Global Launch" and pending validation, i.e. a live QA/dev backlog, not obviously-shipped-and-forgotten. I couldn't confirm any specific open urgent ticket as actually shipped from here, so I *closed none* rather than mark real hotfix work Done on a guess. If you can point me at the ones you're sure shipped, I'll close them out.

Everything durable is in the three ENG tickets (2438/2439/2440) + PR notes so it survives past Slack. Heads-up: #35's token-logging is the item I'd treat as urgent.

*PR #35 "Blake/backend"* — author + merged by *Arthur Blake*; reviewer *Oliver Brooks*. → *ENG-2439*
• Oliver left CHANGES_REQUESTED at 20:36; it was *self-merged 6 minutes later* (21:33), no approval. CodeRabbit also raised security findings.
• *Sitting in the build right now:* `Assets/AWSGameSDK/AWSGameSDKClient.cs` logs the raw login payload — `auth_token`, `refresh_token`, `guest_secret` — to `Debug.LogError` at two spots (the "credentials not set" branch and the `catch`). Any login parse hiccup writes credentials to device logs. Confirmed still on `develop`. `GetUserCountry()` also still crashes on neutral cultures. *This is the one I'd fix before any further release.*
• To be fair: the `DominoPlayerPrefs`→`HarmonyPlayerPrefs` rename Oliver asked for *did* land in a later PR, and the URL-encoding fix landed too.

*PR #26 "cooldown to main menu upgrade ad watch"* — author *[the ads/IAP dev]*; reviewer *Oliver Brooks* (who also merged it). → *ENG-2440*
• Oliver's objection was monetization: the upgrade-ad cooldown resets when the level ends, so a player can *enter a level, lose immediately, return to menu, and re-watch the ad to keep leveling*. Author *argued the point* — deflected to a product call ("@[the PM] said it doesn't matter if you win or lose, we should sync with him"). No sync on the PR, merged anyway, no approval.
• *Sitting in the build:* confirmed in the merge commit — `GameController` resets the cooldown on win *and* `LoseScreen` resets it on loss, so the exploit Oliver flagged is live. Given the game is still taking money, worth a product+eng call on whether reset-on-loss is intended.

*PR #37 "Combo Definition Updates"* — the last thing merged, *2026-02-13*; reviewer *Oliver Brooks*. → *ENG-2438*
• Oliver left CHANGES_REQUESTED (7 inline comments on `ComboDefinition.cs`, `ComboScreen.cs`, `LockedComboCell.cs`, `ComboRarityData/Definition.cs`) — stored `Locked` field, enum naming, an unneeded row class, refactor to a dictionary, and "is this SO even used?". *No approval was ever recorded* before merge the next day.
• *What actually landed:* most of it was fixed anyway — enum became `ERarityEnum`, `IsLocked`/`Level` are computed via `ComboManager`, `LockedComboCell` became `SpecialComboCell` with a `SerializedDictionary`. Two loose ends: the author *argued* the `SpecialComboCell` naming (reviewer never replied), and the `ComboRarityData`/`ComboRarityDefinition` SOs Oliver questioned appear orphaned — the final code uses `ComboLevelUpData` and never references them. Worth confirming they're not dead weight.

────────────────────
*NOT flagged — recorded so the next person can tell the difference:*

*PR #19 "anim sequence on combo changed"* — reviewer *Oliver Brooks*. Oliver flagged a real index-out-of-range bug (`comboTiles[i + 1]` throwing on the last tile). *Nobody said a word back* — no reply, no formal approval — *but the code was actually fixed*: the merged coroutine was refactored so it never does that access. Objection did not survive into the build, so no ticket. Note left on the PR for completeness.

*PR #24 "AppLovinMAX / Rewarded Ads"* — this is the process working. Oliver requested changes twice, author responded, *Oliver APPROVED before it merged*. Left alone.

*On your "worst kind" (agreed-to change that never landed):* I didn't find one. The only clear "yes, I'll change it" agreement was the #35 rename — and that one did eventually land. Good news.

*Also worth knowing:* several sizeable PRs merged with a reviewer *requested but no review ever submitted* — IAP #34, Main Menu #28, Settings #8, combos #3, VFX #33. Not "changes requested," so not ticketed, but nobody actually reviewed them.

────────────────────
*Design-side check (Owen's question — does the spec back up what shipped):*
Short answer: the design docs *don't* back up the rarity/unlock system that shipped. The *Combo Fighter GDD* and the *Combo List* balancing sheet define combos purely by damage multipliers — there is *no* combo-rarity, unlock-cost, or per-rarity level-up spec anywhere in them. The rarity/unlock feature (PR #37) traces only to a "Combo Unlocking Specs" the PR author cited and the Slack rarity thread. And what shipped is `ERarityEnum { Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic }` — 4 tiers, *no Common* — which matches the Slack decision ("common combos = no label, four kinds") but *not* the unlocking spec as paraphrased on the PR, which described a Common tier with its own level-up table. So if the spec got pointed at in a review to justify the rarity behaviour, it doesn't actually say that — the canonical design (GDD/sheet) is silent on rarities entirely.

────────────────────
*Zombie Match board:* I went through it. The urgent items that clearly shipped are *already* Done (e.g. ZOM-291 Time Boosters). The urgent items still *open* are recent (Oct 2025) and sit in Todo / In Progress / Regression / In Validation — labelled "Hot Fix - Global Launch" and pending validation, i.e. a live QA/dev backlog, not obviously-shipped-and-forgotten. I couldn't confirm any specific open urgent ticket as actually shipped from here, so I *closed none* rather than mark real hotfix work Done on a guess. If you can point me at the ones you're sure shipped, I'll close them out.

Everything durable is in the three ENG tickets (2438/2439/2440) + PR notes so it survives past Slack. Heads-up: #35's token-logging is the item I'd treat as urgent.", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0021_SLACK_ID"}}
